records.abstract_evidence_excerpt: The deployment of Large Language Models (LLMs) faces a critical bottleneck when handling lengthy inputs: the prohibitive memory footprint of the Key Value (KV) cache. To address this bottleneck, the token pruning paradigm leverages attention sparsity to selectively retain a small, critical subset of tokens. However, existing approaches fall short, with static methods risking irreversible information loss and dynamic strategies employing heuristics that insufficiently capture the query-dependent nature of token importance. records.title: InfMem: Learning System-2 Memory Control for Long-Context Agent

records.abstract_evidence_excerpt: Reasoning over ultra-long documents requires synthesizing sparse evidence scattered across distant segments under strict memory constraints. While streaming agents enable scalable processing, their passive memory update strategy often fails to preserve low-salience bridging evidence required for multi-hop reasoning. We propose InfMem, a control-centric agent that instantiates System-2-style control via a PreThink-Retrieve-Write protocol. InfMem actively monitors evidence sufficiency, performs targeted in-document retrieval, and applies evidence-aware joint compression to update a bounded memory. records.title: Collaborative deployment of Large AI Models on the edge: A microservice approach to heterogeneous training and quantized inference
records.reason: The edge microservice framework routes quantized model components by precision and QoS across heterogeneous devices; its abstract reports over 70% lower active memory and nearly 60% lower inference latency for edge LAM deployment.
records.source_version: publisher abstract (ScienceDirect; retrieved 2026-10-13)
records.abstract_evidence_excerpt: While Large AI Models (LAMs) offer transformative intelligence, their deployment in real-time Internet-of-Things (IoT) applications is constrained by the heterogeneity of edge networks and high cloud latency. To enable cooperative LAM deployment across diverse edge hardware, we propose a modular, hardware-aware framework. Its precision-aware inference architecture virtualizes model features into multi-precision microservices and dynamically selects variants to balance energy, latency, and accuracy.

records.abstract_evidence_excerpt: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in production, contributing towards shifting the burden in terms of computational resources and energy demands from training to inference. records.abstract_evidence_excerpt: The computing demand of AI is growing at an unprecedented rate, but energy supply is not keeping pace. We find that fine-grained kernel scheduling and frequency scaling jointly and interdependently impact both dynamic and static energy consumption. records.abstract_evidence_excerpt: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to evolve solutions to problems. However, most LLM-evolution frameworks solve static optimization problems, overlooking the open-ended adversarial dynamics that characterize real-world evolutionary processes. Here, we study Digital Red Queen (DRQ), a simple self-play algorithm that embraces these "Red Queen" dynamics via a changing objective. DRQ uses an LLM to evolve assembly programs (warriors) which compete for control of a virtual machine in the game of Core War, a Turing-complete environment studied in artificial life and connected to cybersecurity. records.title: Economical Jet Taggers -- Equivariant, Slim, and Quantized
records.reason: The paper slims and quantizes an equivariant jet-tagging transformer to save compute in particle-physics analysis; the hardware/model-compression connection is plausible, but the abstract does not establish transfer to LLM/VLM inference.
records.source_version: current arXiv abstract-page version at retrieval; version history visible on page where available
records.abstract_evidence_excerpt: Modern machine learning is transforming jet tagging at the LHC, but the leading transformer architectures are large, not particularly fast, and training-intensive. We present a slim version of the L-GATr tagger, reduce the number of parameters of jet-tagging transformers, and quantize them. We compare different quantization methods for standard and Lorentz-equivariant transformers and estimate their gains in resource efficiency. We find an order-of-magnitude reduction in energy cost for an moderate performance decrease, down to 1000-parameter taggers. This might be a step towards trigger-level jet tagging with small and quantized versions of the leading equivariant transformer architectures.

records.abstract_evidence_excerpt: Many state-of-the-art LLMs are trained to think before giving their answer. records.title: Pirate-GPT: A locally deployed large language model framework for reliable offline anti-piracy decision support and knowledge retrieval in maritime operations
records.reason: Pirate-GPT combines semantic sliding-window retrieval, two-stage agent retrieval, and GPTQ local deployment; its intended offline maritime application is explicitly resource-constrained and the abstract identifies quantized deployment.
records.source_version: publisher abstract (ScienceDirect; retrieved 2026-10-13)
records.abstract_evidence_excerpt: Ensuring the reliability and safety of maritime transportation systems is critically impeded by fragmented piracy information. Pirate-GPT is a domain-specific LLM question-answering framework for offline maritime support. Centered on Qwen2.5 and optimized through GPTQ, it supports efficient, stable, privacy-preserving local deployment in resource-constrained environments.

records.title: AdaCodec: A Predictive Visual Code for Video MLLMs
records.reason: AdaCodec predicts visual codes across frames so video MLLMs can avoid re-encoding repeated content; this targets redundant visual tokens and inference cost for video understanding.

records.abstract_evidence_excerpt: Video is temporally redundant: adjacent frames usually share most objects, background, and layout. Yet existing video multimodal large language models (video MLLMs) usually encode each sampled frame as an independent RGB image, causing visual tokens to repeat content already present in earlier frames. This suggests a more direct video interface: send a full reference frame only when the scene cannot be predicted well from prior context, and otherwise transmit a compact description of inter-frame changes.
